extracted.intended_audience: depositors of microorganisms for patent purposes (inventors, patent agents, culture-collection staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Technical and administrative requirements that culture collections impose for making, converting and managing Budapest Treaty deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures, including allowed organism types, sample formats/quantities, testing times, notifications, fees and related procedural forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists which taxa/kinds of biological material the collection accepts for Budapest Treaty patent deposits and explicit exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections specify acceptable types and list exceptions. Examples from the page: VKPM: "Bacteria (including actinomycetes) and microscopic fungi (including yeasts), bacteriophages, plasmids (in host or as an isolated DNA), plant cell cultures, animal and human cell cultures (including hybridoma lines), EXCEPT: microorganisms having properties which are or may be dangerous to health or the environment; microorganisms which need the special containment required for experiments." CCY: "Yeasts which can be stored in liquid nitrogen or as active cultures without any substantial change in their properties." BEA: "Freshwater, marine, hypersaline and soil microalgae and cyanobacteria and marine macroalgae..." CECT: "Bacteria, archaea, filamentous fungi, yeast and plasmids..." IMI: "Nematodes, fungal isolates (including yeasts) and bacteria (including actinomycetes), other than known human and animal pathogens..." Collections reserve the right to refuse material considered an unacceptable risk or technically unsuitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment / Risk-group restrictions (recombinant DNA and pathogens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements limiting deposits to materials not requiring high-level containment or belonging to certain risk groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VKPM: "Deposits containing recombinant DNA molecules must not require physical containment higher than level P2..." CECT: accepts microorganisms up to risk group 3 and excludes certain materials (viruses, bacteriophages, etc.). IMI accepts organisms up to ACDP Category 2. Collections may reject material that presents an unacceptable risk in the Director/Curator's opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity — minimum replicates and preferred formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The acceptable physical form(s) for deposits (lyophilized, frozen, active cultures, purified DNA) and the minimum number of replicates/copies required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different collections specify minima and preferred formats: VKPM prefers lyophilized; minimums: "Fungi, yeasts, bacteria, plasmids (in host) 20 lyophilized cultures or 5 agar cultures; Plasmids (purified DNA) 25 vials (100ng each); Cell lines and hybridomas 25 frozen samples; Bacteriophages 5x0.5ml (free cell lysate) (at least 10^8 pfu/ml)". CCY: "minimum number ... four for lyophilized preparations and two for agar slope cultures." BEA: "minimum number of identical copies ... is five" and specifies cell densities (e.g. 10^2 to 10^4 cells/ml). CECT: "send the CECT five ampoules or agar samples of each strain." IMI: "minimum number of replicates ... should be six." Guidance includes that bacteriophages and plasmids may need to be sent with a suitable host if not available in the collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Required for Viability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Average (and maximum/caveat) times collections require to test viability of deposited material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections publish average and possible extended testing times. Examples: VKPM: "Bacteria, plasmids in hosts 10 days; Fungi, yeasts, bacteriophages, cell lines, hybridomas 20 days." CCY: "average ... six days, but ... may take as long as 14 days." BEA: "average ... seven days, but ... can take up to 35 days." CECT: "bacterial samples is three days (or up to 14 days), and for fungus strains six days (or up to 30 days)." IMI: "average ... 14 days, but ... may take as long as 21 days." Depositors are warned some cases take substantially longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks, renewal of stocks and retention of original material
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on whether collections prepare their own batches, allow depositor authenticity checks, and whether original material is retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most collections prepare batches by subculturing depositor material and require or permit the depositor to test authenticity of batches. VKPM: "prepares the additional samples ... The depositor is entitled to test for authenticity samples from all batches prepared by the VKPM. ... stores a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor, if the culture supplied allows this." CCY: "prepares its own batches ... routinely asks the depositor to check the authenticity ... stores original material." BEA: "prepare its own lots ... depositor will be required to analyze the authenticity of the samples of the first lot ... Except for cryopreserved material, the BEA shall not store the material supplied by the depositor." CECT: "freeze-dries, freezes and retains a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor. The depositor is requested to prove the authenticity of all the freeze-dried and frozen samples prepared by the CECT." IMI: "the depositor is required to test for authenticity samples from all batches ... IMI nevertheless stores a portion of the original material supplied by the depositor."

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Official/accepted languages for communication and documentation with the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VKPM: official language Russian; communications may be exchanged in English. CCY: official language Slovak; communications also accepted in English. BEA: official languages Spanish and English. CECT: official languages Spanish and English. IMI: official language English; communications in any other language are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual terms imposed by deposit application
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal/contractual obligations the depositor accepts by completing the collection's application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common obligations recited include: supply all information requested, pay requisite fees, indemnify the collection against claims (except negligence), not withdraw deposit during required storage period, authorize the collection to supply samples per patent procedure, and replace microorganism at depositor's expense if collection cannot furnish samples. Specific wording: BEA application constitutes a contract and lists these obligations; CECT application is a contract under which depositor undertakes to supply information, pay fees, indemnify, not withdraw, and authorize supply; IMI application form CC PF1 constitutes a contract binding similar obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and/or Quarantine Regulations and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether deposits are subject to import/quarantine rules and whether the collection assists with permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VKPM: "Certain microorganisms ... are subject to import regulations. The VKPM may obtain on behalf of the depositor the necessary import permits; however, the depositor must supply information on the non-pathogenicity ..." CCY: "Import and/or quarantine regulations do not apply to the kinds of microorganisms accepted by the CCY." BEA: "type of organisms accepted ... is not subject to import and/or quarantine regulations." CECT: describes packaging/dispatch rules, notes Spain restrictions on air mail for infectious substances and advises depositors to apply for information. IMI: plant pathogenic fungi not indigenous are subject to import regulations; IMI holds a permit and will advise depositors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to be met by the depositor when making the original deposit (forms and documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative forms and information the depositor must supply when making an original Budapest Treaty deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections require completion of their accession/application form equivalent to model form BP/1 and may require supporting documents. VKPM: complete VKPM-BP/1; CCY: equivalent of model form BP/1; BEA: application and access forms equivalent to BP/1; CECT: equivalent to BP/1; IMI: application form CC PF1 and accession form CC PF2. For later indication/amendment of scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation, collections require model form BP/7 (or equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notifications — use of mandatory international forms (receipts, viability, attestations, furnishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which standard international forms collections issue for receipt, viability statements, attestations and furnishing notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common mandatory forms: BP/4 (receipt), BP/9 (viability statement), BP/8 (attestation of later indication), BP/14 (notification of furnishing samples). Examples: VKPM issues receipt and viability statement on BP/4 and BP/9; CCY issues BP/4 and BP/9 and uses BP/8 and BP/14 for attestation and furnishing; BEA publishes receipt and declaration of viability in BP/4 and BP/9 and uses BP/8 and BP/14 for other notifications; CECT issues BP/4 and BP/9, BP/8 for attestations and BP/14 for furnishing; IMI issues collection-specific versions equivalent to BP/4 and BP/9 (CC PF3, CC PF5) and uses CC PF4 for refusal notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial (provisional) notifications to depositor prior to issuance of official forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and under what conditions collections will provide provisional information (date of deposit, accession number, viability test results) by phone/fax/email prior to official documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices vary: VKPM will telephone/telefax date of deposit and accession number before official receipt only after viability test is done and positive. CCY: does not telephone/telex date/accession or viability before official notifications. BEA: will, if requested, communicate by telephone, fax or electronic mail the date of deposit and entry number after organism received but before official receipt (stating information is provisional), and will also communicate viability analysis results before certificate published. CECT: if requested, communicates date of deposit and accession number by telephone after receipt but before official receipt (provisional); similarly communicates viability results. IMI: acknowledges delivery but does not assign accession until viability confirmed; after positive viability will, if requested, telephone or telex accession and viability before official documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether collection requests/records patent agent contact details and whether it will supply copies of receipt/viability statements to the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VKPM: "If requested, the VKPM supplies copies of the receipt and viability statement to the depositor’s patent agent." CCY: does not routinely ask but will send copies to both depositor and patent agent if requested. BEA: "As a matter of course, the BEA will ask the depositor for the name and address of his patent agent" and will supply copies to both. CECT: routinely asks and supplies copies if requested. IMI: does not routinely ask but will supply copies if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a previous (non-Treaty) deposit to a Budapest Treaty deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which previously made deposits can be converted to Treaty deposits and administrative/fee consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections differ: VKPM: deposits made outside Budapest Treaty may be converted provided originally deposited for patent purposes or confidential for safe-keeping; administrative requirements same as original deposit. CCY: "may be converted ... whether or not they were originally deposited for patent purposes. All conversions are subject to the storage fee ..." BEA: "does not hold deposits made for patent purposes beyond what is stipulated in the Budapest Treaty." CECT: conversions allowed whether or not originally for patent purposes, but previous free deposits become subject to storage fee on conversion; administrative requirements otherwise same. IMI: does not permit conversion of deposits not originally made for patent purposes to Budapest Treaty deposits; deposits previously made for patent purposes outside Treaty may be converted provided depositor supplies a new sample and checks authenticity of all batches; conversions subject to storage fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit (forms and documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative steps and forms required for a new deposit of material already listed or previously deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections require completion of model form BP/2 when making a new deposit and submission of documents specified by Rule 6.2. Receipt and viability statements for new deposits issued on BP/5 and BP/9 (or collection-specific equivalents). Examples: CCY requires BP/2 and BP/5/BP/9; BEA: BP/2 and BP/5/BP/9; CECT: BP/2 and BP/5/BP/9; IMI: requires BP/2 and issues CC PF3/CC PF5 as BP/5/BP/9 equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for samples — third-party request procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: How third parties must request samples from the collection and what documentation/forms are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections advise third parties of correct procedure and, where entitlement/proof is required, provide copies of model request form BP/12 and/or national industrial property office request forms (when collection has them). When responding to overseas requests, collections generally assume the requesting party has met their country's import requirements. IMI does not supply copies of request forms for proof-of-entitlement cases; those must be obtained from the industrial property office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor when samples are furnished to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how depositors are informed when samples are furnished to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard practice is to notify depositors using model form BP/14. Examples: VKPM, CCY, BEA, CECT, IMI notify the depositor on BP/14 (or collection equivalent) each time a sample is furnished to a third party. Some collections also send letters or electronic mail as notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty deposits (publication in collection catalogs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and under what conditions collections list Treaty deposits in their public catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices vary. VKPM: does not list deposits made under the Budapest Treaty in its published catalog. CCY: does not list such deposits in its published catalog. BEA: will publish lists only with written authorization of the depositor. CECT: issues lists in its catalogs only with the express written consent of the depositor. VKPM/other collections may list patents-related deposits (VKPM lists microorganisms that are the subject of granted/published patents of the Russian Federation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees (storage, viability statement, furnishing, communications, other fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee categories charged by collections for storage, issuance of viability statements, furnishing samples, communications/attestations and other services; amounts vary by collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each collection publishes its fee schedule and currency. Examples from the page: NRCA (earlier chunk): Storage 250 USD (30 years), viability 70 USD, furnishing 70 USD, communication 25 USD. VKPM: Storage EUR 500/800 depending on type; viability 100/150; furnishing 100/150; communication 30; other fees according to real cost. CCY: Storage EUR 664; issuance of viability statement 33; furnishing 40. BEA: Storage (cryopreserved) 950 Euros, other methods 3000; publication viability 100; supply samples 60 (plus dispatch cost) / 50; communication amounts listed. CECT: Storage original deposit 600 EUR; new deposits 80 EUR; extension per year 30 EUR; viability 110/45; furnishing 110; communication 110. IMI (UK): Storage 600 GBP; viability 80 GBP; furnishing 55 GBP; attestation 25 GBP; communication 25 GBP. Mailing/dispatch charges generally invoiced separately at cost and fees may be VAT/GST subject to local rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for depositors (availability of standard notes or assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether collections produce standard guidance notes or provide assistance to prospective depositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Varies by collection: NRCA does not produce a standard letter or guidance notes. VKPM: produces notes for guidance of potential depositors. CCY: does not produce standard letter or guidance notes. BEA: No provision. CECT: does not publish specific guidance but will provide information by telephone or correspondence. IMI: makes available detailed notes for the guidance of depositors.
